title: A 2024 station rule gives an uncertain 1.42 rate ratio for strict GMN speed-screen cases in 2025
abstract: We test whether camera station participation predicts extreme meteor speed scores in a later year. A rule fitted only to 29,653 strict shower-assigned GMN events in 2024 flags 26 stations. In 38,516 accepted 2025 events, the rule captures 42 of 270 cases above local solar escape speed by more than five quoted speed errors. The rate ratio after control for shower and month is 1.424, with a conditional 95% date-bootstrap interval of 0.969 to 1.933. Added speed, geometry and station-count controls give 1.408 (0.915 to 2.071). The main test does not establish a persistent station effect. Related threshold checks give mixed precision. These results do not identify a faulty camera or confirm an interstellar meteor. Shared processing, wrong shower labels, station partners and regional selection remain possible causes. Code, selected attributed records, raw source hashes, a figure and reproduction steps are included. No independent instrument reduction of these events was obtained.

display.caption: The 2024 station rule captures 42 of 270 strict 2025 cases. Adjusted rate ratios have date-bootstrap intervals that include one in the main and two control tests.
